data_analysis_project

This is an R Markdown Notebook. When you execute code within the notebook, the results appear beneath the code.

For my data analysis project, I will be working with Clergy Contributions data from 2018-2024 and the Maryland campaign contributions data.

##Loading libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(janitor)
library(ggthemes)
library(tidycensus)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(tigris)
library(sf)

–> question 1: <- Do the top clergy donors also give to Maryland state campaigns?

##getting the data

clergy_contribs_2018 <- read_csv("data/clergy_contribs_2018.csv")
clergy_contribs_2020 <- read_csv("data/clergy_contribs_2020.csv")
clergy_contribs_2022 <- read_csv("data/clergy_contribs_2022.csv")
clergy_contribs_2024 <- read_csv("data/clergy_contribs_2024.csv")
md_campaign <- read_csv("~/Downloads/md_contribs.csv.zip")

Cleaning up the clergy contributions data and combining all of the dataframes into one. This code block also includes cleaning up the data.

clergy_contribs_combined <- bind_rows(list(clergy_contribs_2018, clergy_contribs_2020, clergy_contribs_2022, clergy_contribs_2024)) |>
  mutate(contributor_first_name = str_to_upper(contributor_first_name), contributor_last_name = str_to_upper(contributor_last_name), contributor_name = str_to_upper(contributor_name), contributor_city = str_to_upper(contributor_city), 
         zip5 = str_sub(contributor_zip, start=1L, end=5L)) 
       

View(clergy_contribs_combined)
clergy_totals <- clergy_contribs_combined |>
  group_by(contributor_name,two_year_transaction_period) |>
  summarize(
    total_amount = sum(contribution_receipt_amount),
    num_contributions = n(),
  ) |>
arrange(desc(total_amount))

clergy_totals

Searching for the top donors in the md_campaign database

d_cowan_state <- md_campaign |> 
  filter(contributor_first_name == "DORIS", contributor_last_name == "COWAN") 
         
j_price <- md_campaign |> 
  filter(contributor_first_name == "JOHN", contributor_last_name == "PRICE")

a_fraser <- md_campaign |> 
  filter(contributor_first_name == "ALEXA", contributor_last_name == "FRASER")

d_sword <- md_campaign |> 
  filter(contributor_first_name == "DAVID", contributor_last_name == "SWORD")

l_mann <- md_campaign |> 
  filter(contributor_first_name == "LUCRETIA", contributor_last_name == "MANN")

e_spearman <- md_campaign |> 
  filter(contributor_first_name == "ELDRIDGE", contributor_last_name == "SPEARMAN")

Explanation #1

So far, I think I found some baseline results needed to answer my question of wo the top donors are and whether they contribute to Maryland campaigns. I have calculated the total amount contributed by a two year transaction period for the entire data frame. The results of this show that John Price has donated contributed twice among the top contributors, and Doris Cowan as the top contributor. After I found these top donors within the clergy contribution data, I used the Maryland campaign contribution website to search for the names listed under the top 10 clergy contributors, and six of the ten contributors were listed once or multiple times. I think my next step is to get a hold of the campaign data to further confirm that these clergy contributors have donated to Maryland campaigns. One thing that I think will be an issue is the timeframes of my data frames, whereas I have information for clergy contributions for 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024, so I will need these years for campaign contribution data. Of the top ten clergy members, the majority of them appear in the Maryland campaigns data frame. Many of the clergy that have contributed to Maryland campaigns have only contributed one time compared to the several contributions made in the clergy data frame. One of the most significant donors in this data is from Doris Cowan, who contributed over 6,000 times in the clergy database, and 25 times in the Maryland campaign data. According to a document from the General Commissioners From Presbytery of Baltimore in 2020, Cowan is honorably retired. Looking at all of the contributions made in the clergy contributions data and the Maryland campaign data, Cowan has contributed money to democratic organizations and campaigns. In comparison to Doris Cowan, the other contributors have only contributed once or twice, such as Alexa Fraser, who contributed twice this year. I think Doris Cowan is an obvious outlier in the data of Maryland campaign contributions. Since they are a retired clergy member, this could indicate that they have signed up for recurring payments unknowingly, or they are just more politically active following retirement.

Another thing that I find interesting is that majority of these clergy members have donated to Maryland campaigns, even if it was only once. I find this interesting because we often assume those within the church environment do not affiliate themselves with politics of any sort. Another interesting factor is that these members have only contributed to campaigns within the last few years, 2024-2026, which could possibly suggest that these clergy members are becoming more politically active as the nation becomes increasingly politically polarized.

Creating Cowan dataframes for state and federal contributions + making a bar chart


d_cowan_state <- d_cowan_state |>
  mutate(contributor_name = paste(contributor_last_name, contributor_first_name, sep = ", ")) |>
  rename(contribution_receipt_amount = transaction_amount,
         contribution_receipt_date = transaction_date)
cowan_federal <- clergy_contribs_combined |> 
  filter(contributor_name == "COWAN, DORIS") |> 
  select(contributor_name, contribution_receipt_amount)

cowan_comparison <- bind_rows(
  cowan_federal |>
    summarise(total_amount = sum(contribution_receipt_amount)) |>
    mutate(source = "Federal"),
  d_cowan_state |>
    summarise(total_amount = sum(contribution_receipt_amount)) |>
    mutate(source = "State")
)

cowan_comparison |>
  ggplot(aes(x = source, y = total_amount)) +
  geom_col(fill = "lightpink") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme_fivethirtyeight() +
  labs(
    title = "How One Clergy Member Allocated Maryland Political Contributions",
    x = "Contribution Source",
    y = "Total Contributions"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold")
  )

Next, I want to look at party affiliations based on the committee that the clergy member contributed to. Using a database from Joe Wicke, each committee is assigned either a D or R.

#Loading in data that has the committee party affiliations

committee_parties <- read_csv("data/committee_parties_clean.csv")
clergy_contribs_combined_with_parties <- clergy_contribs_combined |> 
  inner_join(committee_parties, join_by(committee_name))

clergy_contribs_combined_with_parties |> 
  group_by(party) |> 
  summarize(total_amount = sum(contribution_receipt_amount, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(desc(total_amount))

Since Maryland is a democratic state, the results for the total amounts contributed to democratic versus republican committees make sense.

question 2 –> Which cities in Maryland have the highest clergy contributions?

top_cities <- clergy_contribs_combined |> 
  group_by(contributor_city) |>
  summarise(total_amount = sum(contribution_receipt_amount, na.rm = TRUE), total_contribs = n()) |>
  arrange(desc(total_amount)) |> 
  mutate(contributor_city = trimws(contributor_city)) |> 
  filter(total_amount > 1500.00)
top_cities
write_csv(top_cities, "top_cities.csv")

top_cities <- read_csv("top_cities.csv")

Say that you used chat to get the columns right lmao

md_cities <- get_acs(
  geography = "place",
  variables = c(
    median_income = "B19013_001",
    population = "B01003_001"
  ),
  year = 2021,
  state = "MD",
  geometry = TRUE
) |>
  select(NAME, variable, estimate, geometry) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = variable,
    values_from = estimate
  )
md_cities <- md_cities |>
  mutate(NAME = str_to_title(str_remove_all(NAME, ", Maryland"))) |>
  mutate(NAME = str_to_upper(NAME)) |>
  mutate(NAME = str_remove_all(NAME, " CDP")) |>
  mutate(NAME = str_remove_all(NAME, " TOWN")) |>
  mutate(NAME = str_remove_all(NAME, " CITY")) |>
  mutate(NAME = str_remove_all(NAME, " VILLAGE")) |>
  mutate(NAME = trimws(NAME))

##Combining the top cities dataframe with the md_cities_pop dataframe.

md_city_contribs <- md_cities |>
  inner_join(top_cities, join_by(NAME == contributor_city)) |> 
  mutate(contribs_rate_pop = total_amount/population*10000,
         contribs_rate_income = total_amount/median_income*10000) |> 
  arrange(desc(total_amount)) 

top_cities |>
  anti_join(md_cities, join_by(contributor_city == NAME))
NA

##Making Map

For this section, I got the outline for Maryland counties, using the counties <- counties() to get all U.S. counties, then filtered for Maryland only counties in the following line. Then, I created a map using the weight as the total_amount from the md_city_contribs dataframe. This provided a map of the cities that have contributed the most to least within the state of Maryland.

counties <- counties()

md_counties <- counties |>
  filter(STATEFP == "24")


ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data=md_counties) + 
  geom_sf(data=md_city_contribs, aes(fill=contribs_rate_pop)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_viridis_b(option="magma",trans = "log") + 
  labs(title = "Maryland Clergy Contributions by population")

counties <- counties()

md_counties <- counties |>
  filter(STATEFP == "24")


ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data=md_counties) + 
  geom_sf(data=md_city_contribs, aes(fill=contribs_rate_income)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_viridis_b(option="magma",trans = "log") + 
  labs(title = "Maryland Clergy Contributions by income")

Map is concentrated in the suburban/urban areas of Maryland, mainly around Prince George’s County, Montgomery County and Baltimore.
